newsitem.title: VENEZUELA: Venezuela restricts tanker traffic after grounding.
newsitem.headline: Venezuela restricts tanker traffic after grounding.

text.p: Venezuela's port authority in Maracaibo said on Tuesday it had restricted the flow of tankers through its navigation channel following the grounding of two oil tankers in the last two weeks.
"The traffic is restricted to those with less than 38 feet (11.5 meter) of draught," Maracaibo Port Captain Regulo Dominguez told Reuters in a brief telephone interview.

Dominguez said the new restriction had been enforced after the Greek-flagged tanker Olympic Sponsor ran aground late Monday in the outer navigation channel of Lake Maracaibo in northwestern Venezuela. The tanker was en route to Rotterdam with 477,000 barrels of medium crude on board.
Attempts to re-float the tanker have so far been unsuccessful and authorities were waiting for new equipment to arrive before trying again.
"The operation to re-float the tanker have been suspended for the moment," Dominguez said.
A shipping agent in Maracaibo said the Olympic Sponsor had a draught of 39 feet but that the 38 feet restriction was unlikely to affect oil exports from Lake Maracaibo.

The tanker had run into difficulties between buoys 20 and 22 of the navigation channel -- exactly the same place where the Greek-flagged Nissos Amorgos tanker ran aground Feb. 28 spilling at least 28,000 barrels of heavy crude.
The Olympic Sponsor had left state oil company Lagoven's La Salina port on the northeastern shore of Lake Maracaibo earlier Monday.
